## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="design-interface-review" -->
Post-deploy live check for LIN-4380 (P2 of LIN-4349, merged c998cf4c, deployed): a converted corrective template must file no tickets; one docs-only PR touching docs/reviews and docs/areas; objective breakage in the closing comment. Record the run on LIN-4380 and LIN-4349.

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

# Design & Interface Review — periodical run (tenth)

This is the tenth run of the Design & Interface Review and the **first under the converted template** (LIN-4380, merged `c998cf4c`): it feeds the area notes and **mints no tickets**. The operator note above makes this run the live witness for that change. When you conclude, also post a short comment on **LIN-4380** and on **LIN-4349** that says: how many issues this run created besides itself (it should be zero), the docs-only PR number and the paths it touched, and whether the closing comment lists objective breakage.

The evidence for this review is the **rendered product**: what a user sees on screen. Every other review reads code or history. This one looks at the running app.

## Grounding (what minting found at `c998cf4c`, 8 Nov 2026; re-check it all live)

* **Prior runs.** Reports are in `docs/reviews/`, named `design-interface-review-<date>.md`, with evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>/`. The last one is `design-interface-review-2026-10-21.md` (run 9, LIN-3747). It measured window `6e8bf424..0b4bd287`, so **this run's window is** `0b4bd287..HEAD`. Read it first, especially §3 (the re-measure), §6 (coverage limits), §9 (follow-ups) and §10 (advisory tail). Earlier reports from 06-20 to 09-26 are in the same folder.
* **What happened to run 9's tickets** (status at minting): LIN-3761 (Library table clip), LIN-3762 (archive muted tier), LIN-3763 (dark UA links and native controls), LIN-3119 (dark `.action-btn`), LIN-739 (landing CTA teal) and LIN-3121 (upstream error prose) are **Done**, so re-measure each one on fresh renders and confirm the fix held. **Still open:** LIN-3123 (status and fill colours used as text, light theme), LIN-3120 (Ship has no headings), LIN-849 (focus-ring and CTA a11y), LIN-3760 (test seam: non-Linear merge consent only renders synthetically). Run 9's advisory tail items A1–A8 were not ticketed. Check which of them the UI work since then addressed.
* **The window is large and mostly UI.** About 417 product files changed in `0b4bd287..c998cf4c`. Mapped through `docs/areas/areas.json`: front-end-pages 74, front-end-browser 73 (36 stylesheets under `public/`, including `style.css` and `styleguide.css`), runs-and-dispatch 75, llm-and-prompts 51, web-routes 37, auth-accounts-and-workspaces 33. This came from the UI passage (LIN-3490 charter), the UI finish series (LIN-4008, LIN-4011–LIN-4014, some still open), the UI sweep (LIN-3892), the home and type rebuilds (LIN-4024, LIN-4103–LIN-4117) and the designer's gap review `docs/reviews/ui-design-gap-review-2026-10-26/`. Look first at the pages that work landed on.
* **Visual capture.** `playwright.visual.config.js` runs `tests/visual/*.spec.js` against a test server on :3001 (no PAT, empty DB). It writes PNGs and asserts nothing. Authenticated views go through the test-session seam (`/test/set-session` and `/test/set-local-session` in `routes/test.js`, wrapped by `createSession()` in `tests/helpers.js`). Flagged and experimental views are reached through the feature parameters (`featuresParam()`; see `docs/view-tiers.md`). Run 9's own capture, census and re-measure scripts are in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-21/capture/`, so reuse them rather than rebuilding. **Never trust committed renders** (`tests/screenshots/`, earlier evidence folders, the gap review's `shots/`). They lag the live UI. Regenerate everything.
* **Design-system baseline.** `/styleguide` (`lib/render-styleguide.js`, `public/styleguide.css`) is the committed token reference and visual baseline. Open baseline defects: LIN-3957 and LIN-3960. Run 9 found that its dark swatches carry light hex captions.
* **Known-issue tickets to cite, not re-flag:** LIN-3802 (Markdown tables in descriptions have no scroll wrapper), LIN-3803 (archives 5–9 non-muted contrast), LIN-3997 (`/privacy` and `/terms` ignore a dark system theme), LIN-4339 (a Library figure panel stays light in dark mode), LIN-2740 (rulings touch targets), LIN-1574, LIN-1584, LIN-1018, LIN-2491/2492, LIN-916, LIN-1688.
* **Area notes.** Rules: `docs/areas/README.md`. Registry: `docs/areas/areas.json` (first match wins). Guard: `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (6144-byte cap per note, the first cited path must map to the note's area, and cited paths must exist). Notes exist for front-end-browser, web-routes and others. **front-end-pages has no note yet**, so if a finding binds there, create `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md` following the README. Note: `llm-and-prompts.md` and `runs-and-dispatch.md` are already close to the cap.
* **Conventions.** Branch off `main`. `ci-success` must be green before merge (CLAUDE.md). Prior design reports trimmed their evidence to about 10 MB or less, kept JSON and the capture scripts, and dropped PNGs the report doesn't cite (run 9 §8). Do the same.
* **Merge authority.** LIN-4390 (open) records that the template's "merge your own PR" can conflict with the dispatch gate, which reserves merge for review and close-out. If the gate refuses your merge, that is the "genuinely impossible" case below: name the blocker in the closing comment as an explicit handoff.

## Review contract

**Audit the scope before you start.** The scope above is a starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside. Before running the review, look for surfaces this review should cover that the scope does not name, and fold them in. For example: pages added since run 9, flagged views, error and empty states, emails, guest share links, the run-9 §6 limits still carried, and seams no sibling review owns. If you could only shrink a scope, be suspicious of it. The expected move is to widen it to what the remit reaches. Be **broad in discovery but bounded in output**. Widening changes what you examine, not what you report. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked, and a clean, near-empty result is a genuine outcome. Area-note entries stay within their bound: add one only where a finding binds a builder or leaves work waiting in an area, and keep each note under its cap.

**Read prior runs first.** Read the earlier reports and focus on what is still open or was never reached. Build on them. Don't re-derive the same report or re-flag what's already handled.

**Render, don't read.** Run the repo's own visual-capture mechanism to make fresh full-page renders of every user-facing surface at desktop and mobile widths, in both themes. Authenticate through the test or mock-session seam for views that need a session. Add an accessibility pass and a performance pass with the browser tooling available (run 9 used Lighthouse plus a computed-contrast census). Regenerate everything at run time, and treat all committed reference renders as stale. Measure what you see against the app's own `/styleguide` page to answer: does the UI actually use its own design system? Run 9 carried two cautions. Pages that honour the `theme` cookie ignore `prefers-color-scheme`, so set the cookie for dark captures. And `overflow-x: clip` makes `scrollWidth` useless as proof of no overflow, so use element geometry.

**Required section: first experience.** Every run must have an explicit section on a cold visitor's first experience. It must cover:

* whether it is clear what the product is and how it works;
* how onboarding and first run feel;
* how empty states read;
* whether the single primary call-to-action has the affordance it deserves, or is disguised among lower-stakes chrome.

This section also carries the verdict on **aesthetic coherence and first impression**: in the first \~5 seconds, does the surface look trustworthy, polished and intentional? Does the CLI/terminal look read as a deliberate, well-executed design language, or as an accidental default? Keep this section even when the rest of the report is short.

**Interface finding classes.** Assess:

* visual consistency against the design system (shared tokens for colour, spacing, type and state indicators, or hardcoded one-offs);
* accessibility (contrast, focus order, keyboard reach, alt text, ARIA and semantics);
* responsive and mobile (layout integrity and overflow);
* affordance and discoverability (systemic low affordance, especially on first-run surfaces, is a first-class concern; weigh it honestly against the deliberate minimal aesthetic);
* information hierarchy;
* copy and labelling (each destination named the same everywhere).

These classes are **examples, not a limit**. Find the complete set for this remit in the repo. The list is a floor to build on, not a ceiling.

**Design-quality finding classes.** This is a proactive read on how to make the UI look better, judged *within* the minimal CLI/terminal idiom and never as a push toward generic chrome. Assess:

* visual hierarchy and emphasis, the eye-path (a clear first, second and third read; a dominant primary action; size, weight and colour ranking content in a flat monospace design). This is the highest-leverage dimension.
* layout, spacing and alignment rhythm (a spacing scale, shared edges, whitespace that groups and separates on purpose);
* typography (a real type scale, line length, line height, weight and case doing hierarchy work);
* colour and palette as design (cohesion, restraint, and consistent semantic use of accent and the ✓ ◐ ○ state colours);
* polish and craft details (borders, dividers, box-drawing rules, indicator sizing, hover, focus and active states, transitions);
* aesthetic coherence and first-impression quality (this goes in the first-experience section).

These findings feed the advisory tail, never the objective-breakage route.

**Mind the altitude.** This review owns the rendered product. Leave code and stylesheet structure to the Code Quality Review, HTTP and interface contracts to the API Quality Review, documentation prose to the Documentation Review, and whether the onboarding journey completes to Onboarding & Cold-Start. Cite them only where a visible defect traces back to their territory, and let them own the fix.

**Uncapped report.** Write a clear, severity-ranked report of everything found. Run 9's S1–S4 scale is a good default. Nothing, one thing or many are all valid results. Don't pad. Ground every finding in this run's fresh renders. Save the report at `docs/reviews/design-interface-review-<run date>.md` with its evidence in `docs/reviews/_evidence-<run date>/`. That is the convention found. Confirm it before writing. If no such place existed, the report would go in this task's own comment instead.

**Feed the area notes. Mint no follow-up tasks.** Follow the area notes' own rules (the registry, the note format, the guard, the byte cap, and one home for each leftover; `LEFTOVER_RULE` is in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`). Start from the files changed between `0b4bd287` and HEAD, map each one to its area through the registry, and look first where work landed. In each note you touch, prune entries that are settled or no longer true, and keep the note under its cap. For a finding that leaves work in an area, add a **Waiting** entry. For a rule a builder there must follow, add a **Lesson**. Each entry cites the file it is about first, then names this reading as its source ("Design & Interface Review, <run date>"), with this report as the second cited path. A finding already filed as a ticket stays in the report only, never also in a note. Commit the report and the note edits together in **one docs-only pull request**. Rebase it onto main, get it green under the notes guard and the required checks, and merge it under the merge authority the second-read section below gives you.

**Route each finding that has no area note to the person, never to a ticket.**

* *A larger tidy* (a move bigger than a change should take on in passing): write it as a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and also list it for the person in the closing comment.
* *A finding with no area file to cite* (dependency manifests, lockfiles, urgent breakage such as a live secret): put it in the closing comment, addressed to the person.
* *A cross-area seam*: file it under the area a change would start from, name the other side, and say plainly in the report that seams have no full home in the notes yet.
* *A repo with no area notes*: keep every finding in the report and the closing comment only.

**Route objective breakage to the person, never to a ticket.** List each objective breakage for the person in the closing comment, ranked by severity: a contrast failure, a mobile overflow, a broken or unusable layout. Where it traces to a file in an area, also add it to that area's note. This route never covers a subjective design call.

**Keep subjective design direction advisory, but make the tail actionable.** Aesthetic, tone, layout taste, the minimalism-versus-discoverability tension, and everything from the design-quality classes go in the report's **advisory tail**. Write it as a **ranked shortlist of the highest-impact visual improvements**. Each item is a concrete *before → after* within the CLI/terminal idiom, measured against `/styleguide`. Order it so a maintainer can read the top item, say yes, and promote it into an implementation task. "This surface already looks good as-is" is a valid, explicit conclusion.

**Then conclude this task. Do not leave it open.** Post a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report as a comment on this task. Include the report's path, name the docs-only PR, and list for the person any larger tidy, any finding with no area file to cite, and the objective breakage. Then move the task to Done. A review task left open is re-recommended forever.

**Stay review-only.** Change no code, config or secrets, and no docs except the report, its evidence folder and the area-note edits. Capturing renders and running accessibility and performance passes is inspection, not a change to ship. An operator instruction not to touch files covers the code and docs under review. It does not cover this task's own report and note edits.

**Fresh-context adversarial second-read: required before Done.** After the report and note edits are written, and before the Done transition can succeed, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"* Use **Tier 1** (preferred: a wholly separate session with no memory of this run) or **Tier 2** (accepted fallback: a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn). **Tier 3**, this same session re-reading its own report, is **not accepted**. State which tier you used.

Then post **one comment** on this task that holds all three fields together in one body:

* `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
* `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO` (whether the reader's answer differed from the report's top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict)
* `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`

The engine reads that comment and refuses a premature Done until all three fields appear together in one comment body. Copy the same three fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier, the question and the reader's full answer. AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude the task normally: a DISAGREE is itself the escalation.

This task owns merging its own report PR. Once the PR's required checks are green, merge it before Done. The report is docs-only, so merging it yourself is safe. Only when merging is genuinely impossible (no merge permission, a gate refusal, or required checks still red) may the task conclude with the PR open. In that case, name the blocker in the closing comment as an explicit handoff, never as ordinary completion.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Research findings (8 Nov 2026, research stage)

Full notes, with a brief and sources for each layer, are in the research comment of 8 Nov. This section holds what the plan needs.

**Grounding holds.** HEAD = `c998cf4c5`, the mint SHA. Nothing has changed since the ticket was created. The window `0b4bd287..c998cf4c` has 419 commits and 417 product files, and the per-area counts match the ticket exactly.

### Key findings

1. **Run 9's tooling works at HEAD once it is ported.** In the spike, `boot-3199.mjs` booted HEAD, and `capture.mjs` rendered 24/24 states (landing, styleguide, and authenticated settings, dispatch and tree, both themes) in 12.7 s. The scripts resolve paths relative to their own folder and import product code relatively, so the copy must sit at `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-08/capture/`. Edits it needs: `build-registry.mjs` `PRIOR` → `0b4bd287`; `renderer-args.mjs` `TIME`; curated rows for the new routes; drop `next-run`; sample args for 3 new renderers; the Lighthouse path (`beat2.mjs` hardcodes another machine's npx path, so use `npx lighthouse@12.8.2`).
2. **New surfaces since run 9:** `/getting-started`, `/workspace/:urlKey/backlog`, `/workspace/:urlKey/settings/:area`. `/workspace/:urlKey/next-run` was removed. There are 20 new front-end-pages components (Settings rebuild, decision panel, halt controls, tabs, head-meta and og-image).
3. **The grounding missed run 9's two "first candidates next run":** finding 29 (unnamed controls on Settings and Proxy; re-measure on the rebuilt Settings) and finding 30 (`/swipe` `user-scalable=no`, **still in source** at `lib/render-swipe.js`). Neither was ticketed, so under the converted template both are objective breakage: they go to the closing comment and to a note.
4. **Re-measure ledger:** 6 Done tickets to confirm (LIN-3761, 3762, 3763, 3119, 739, 3121) and open ones to cite (LIN-3123, 3120, 849, 3760, plus the known-issue list). LIN-849 is still open after LIN-739, so measure the teal on every door. "A1–A8" is read as run 9 §10 items 1–8, and the report should say so.
5. **Notes:** front-end-pages has no note, so create `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md` if a finding binds there. `llm-and-prompts.md` (6118 B) and `runs-and-dispatch.md` (6056 B) are almost full. A defect on a page owned by in-flight UI tickets (LIN-4008 and its children, LIN-4011 to LIN-4014, LIN-3892) stays in the report only.
6. **Merge:** LIN-4390 is unresolved. Follow the LIN-4387 precedent: build opens the PR green, review approves, close-out merges pinned. The As-asked block's handoff clause covers this, so it is **not a cut**.
7. **Witness measurement:** a raw count of new issues gives a false red, because LIN-4381 and the coordinator file in parallel. Use each session's own `GET /api/proxy/credential-trail` count of `POST /api/proxy/issues`, which should be 0; this research session's count is 0. Add a check that no `gh issue create` was run. Baseline: LIN-4391 is the newest identifier, so attribute each issue from LIN-4392 onward to its lane at close.

### Classes

* **Surfaces (bounded by** `build-registry.mjs` **at HEAD; my route-diff grep agrees):** 150 registry entries and 55 page GET destinations. Differences: unmapped `/getting-started`, `/workspace/:urlKey/backlog`, `/workspace/:urlKey/settings/:area`; stale `/workspace/:urlKey/next-run`; renderers with no sample args `renderPlainPage`, `renderSignInUnavailablePage`, `renderSourceErrorPage`; the live-console experimental-tag mismatch against `EXPERIMENTAL_VIEWS`. Plus 9 archives, `/archive/999`, Library documents (enumerated at census time), 13 email renderers, 27 intercepted renderers and 8 intercepted states.
* **Re-measure set:** LIN-3761, 3762, 3763, 3119, 739, 3121 (Done); LIN-3123, 3120, 849, 3760 (open); run 9 findings 29 and 30; run 9 §10 items 1–8; the open baseline tickets LIN-3957 and 3960.
* **Changed files by area:** 417, mapped as in the ticket's grounding (13 areas).
* **Issue-creation channels for the witness:** proxy `POST /api/proxy/issues` (per-token trail) and `gh issue create`. These are all the channels a session has.
* **Unbounded (named):** live KPI populations, real upstream outages and real review bodies are production data, not source, so they stay synthetic or seeded and labelled. Non-Linear merge consent is synthetic only (`/test/set-merge-conflict-session` seeds only `linear`; LIN-3760).

### Recommended approach

Two build beats on one branch and one docs-only PR:

* **Beat 1, measure:** port the tooling with the edits above; registry; full capture at 1400/390 × light/dark (cookie-driven dark, geometry overflow rule), plus 320 for cold and changed surfaces; census; Lighthouse on cold surfaces plus about 6 authenticated ones; re-measure the whole set; commit the evidence and `coverage-map.md`.
* **Beat 2, judge:** image-read the new and changed surfaces closely and sample the carried ones; write `docs/reviews/design-interface-review-2026-11-08.md` (S1–S4, required first-experience section, advisory tail as before → after); add the note entries (area file first, report second, "Design & Interface Review, 8 Nov."); run the guard plus a mutation check; run a Tier-2 second-read and post the three-field comment; trim the evidence to about 10 MB or less; get the PR green.
* **Then review → close-out:** close-out merges, posts the closing comment (objective breakage ranked, larger tidies, no-area findings), posts the LIN-4380 and LIN-4349 witness comments (0 issues, the PR number and paths, whether objective breakage is listed), and moves the ticket to Done.

Surface Assessment: \[improvement noticed, not required: per-run copies of the capture tooling drift (PRIOR sha, TIME, curated routes); a durable home would remove that drift. Note it in the report or as a size-of-move Waiting entry. This run changes no code.\]

No cut to the As-asked block is proposed.

## Implementation Plan

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The ticket asks for the tenth Design & Interface Review of the rendered product (window `0b4bd287..HEAD`) and, because it is the first run under the converted template (LIN-4380, `c998cf4c`), for it to be the live witness of that change: **feed the area notes, mint no tickets, one docs-only PR, objective breakage in the closing comment**, plus witness comments on LIN-4380 and LIN-4349.

Done, as the person who asked would check it (the ticket has no Done-when of its own; this one is the plan's, written from the As-asked block):

1. `docs/reviews/design-interface-review-2026-11-08.md` exists, severity-ranked (S1–S4), with the required first-experience section, the re-measure ledger, coverage limits, an advisory tail of ranked before → after items, and the `## Adversarial Second-Read` section. Evidence is in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-08/` at 10 MB or less, with the capture scripts and JSON kept.
2. One docs-only PR holds the report, its evidence and the note edits, and touches only `docs/reviews/` and `docs/areas/`. The area-notes guard and `ci-success` are green on it.
3. Zero issues were created by this run's lanes, shown by per-session proxy trail counts (see Witness).
4. The closing comment lists objective breakage ranked, larger tidies, and findings with no area file; the LIN-4380 and LIN-4349 comments carry the three facts the ticket names.

**Cuts to the As-asked block: none.** Every sentence is delivered in full. The merge clause is delivered by its own handoff wording (see Merge), so it is not a cut. Nothing in the ask has drifted from its purpose.

### Re-grounding (read at HEAD, not from research prose)

* Local `main` is `c998cf4c5`, the mint SHA; `git log --since=2026-11-08T14:13:42Z -- lib routes public server.js docs/reviews docs/areas` is empty. Research's grounding holds. The build must still re-check HEAD first; if `main` moved, recompute the window and counts, never reuse research's.
* `lib/render-swipe.js:144` still has `user-scalable=no` (run 9 finding 30). `docs/areas/areas.json` maps `lib/render-*.js`, `lib/components/*`, `settings-areas` and `settings-copy-first-card` to `front-end-pages`; `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md` does not exist. `docs/areas/` holds nine notes; `llm-and-prompts.md` is 6118 B and `runs-and-dispatch.md` is 6056 B against a 6144 B cap.
* Run 9's tooling is 26 files in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-21/capture/`. `build-registry.mjs:29` pins `PRIOR='6e8bf424'`; `renderer-args.mjs:15` pins `TIME='2026-10-21…'`. The scripts resolve paths from their own directory, so they only work at `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>/capture/`.

### Route: how the change goes, and what was set aside

Two build sessions on **one branch and one PR**, then review and close-out under the dispatch gate.

* **Session 1 — Measure.** Port the tooling, regenerate everything, commit evidence JSON and `coverage-map.md`. No judging yet.
* **Session 2 — Judge and deliver.** Image-read, write the report and notes, mutation-check the guard, run the independent second-read, trim evidence, open the PR green.

Set aside: (a) one session for everything, because the image-read of hundreds of renders is the part that degrades into a templated read (run 9 §6 admits its sub-reader lines were pointers, not measurements); (b) run 9's six beats, because they existed to carry minting and the three-mint cap, which the converted template removes; (c) a durable home for the capture tooling, because this run changes no code. That is recorded as a size-of-move Waiting entry (see Notes) rather than done.

### Session 1: Measure (behaviour required, builder writes the code)

1. **Port** `capture/` to `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-08/capture/` (same depth). Set `PRIOR` to `0b4bd287`, update `TIME`. Replace the hardcoded Lighthouse path in `beat2.mjs` with `LIGHTHOUSE_CLI` or `npx lighthouse@12.8.2` (the version run 9 used, for comparability).
2. **Registry must cover the live route set.** Add curated rows for `/getting-started`, `/workspace/:urlKey/backlog` and `/workspace/:urlKey/settings/:area` (areas enumerated from `lib/settings-areas.js`, never hand-listed); drop `/workspace/:urlKey/next-run` from registry rows and capture keys (deleted in the window); give sample args to `renderPlainPage`, `renderSignInUnavailablePage`, `renderSourceErrorPage`; reconcile live-console's experimental tag with `EXPERIMENTAL_VIEWS`. **Witness for "every place found":** the registry's own `differences` list must be empty or each remaining difference explained in `coverage-map.md`. Research saw 150 entries and 55 page destinations; these are expectations to regenerate, not facts to copy. Also enumerate the nine archives, `/archive/999`, Library documents, the email renderers and the intercepted renderers and states at census time; an independent route grep (`router|app.get` against `0b4bd287`) is the cross-check, as research did.
3. **Capture** at 1400 and 390 px in both themes (dark by setting the `theme` cookie, because app pages ignore `prefers-color-scheme`), plus 320 px for cold and changed surfaces. Authenticated views through `/test/set-session` and `/test/set-local-session`; flagged views through `featuresParam()`. Seed states from `tests/visual/lin-4024-*` and `lin-4103…lin-4117-*` specs but never use their committed PNGs. The social card `public/logo/og-image.png` is read directly (viewport captures do not show it).
4. **Measure with geometry, not** `scrollWidth` (`overflow-x: clip` makes it vacuous). `/styleguide` at 390 px gave `bodyOver: 1` with no offender in the spike: verify sub-pixel before calling it overflow. Colour comes from capture JSON, never from quantised PNGs.
5. **Census and Lighthouse:** computed-contrast census on every capture; Lighthouse on cold surfaces and about six authenticated ones.
6. **Re-measure ledger**, each row a fresh render with a verdict "held / regressed / still open": Done tickets LIN-3761, 3762, 3763, 3119, 739, 3121; open LIN-3123, 3120, 849 (measure the teal CTA on **every** entry surface, not only landing), 3760, 3957, 3960; run 9 finding 29 (unnamed controls, on **every** rebuilt `settings/:area` page and Proxy) and finding 30 (`/swipe` zoom); run 9 §10 items 1–8, read as the eight numbered advisory items there, not the older A-IDs reused in §3 (the report states this reading). Cite, do not re-flag, the known-issue list in the ticket.
7. **Name the limits, never fake them** in `coverage-map.md`: non-Linear merge consent is synthetic only (`/test/set-merge-conflict-session` seeds only Linear; LIN-3760); live KPI populations, real upstream outages and real review bodies are seeded or synthetic; the task page under the Linear mock; and, to be **determined in this session**, how far sent-email and live-data guest-share links can be reached (research did not check). Whatever is unreachable is stated as a limit.
8. **Witness for session 1:** capture runs report 0 failures and the number of states rendered equals the registry's expected count; `verify-report-figures.mjs` (carried) passes on the metrics JSON; the commit is pushed to the branch before the session ends.

### Session 2: Judge and deliver

1. **Read, don't skim.** Image-read every new or changed surface closely (the 20 new front-end-pages components and Settings rebuild, backlog, getting-started, decision panel, halt controls, tabs, head-meta/og-image) and a recorded sample of carried surfaces; the report says which were read and which were measured only. Look first where work landed (the area mapping of the changed files).
2. **Report** at `docs/reviews/design-interface-review-2026-11-08.md`: S1–S4 findings; first-experience section (product clarity, onboarding, empty states, primary-CTA affordance, first-five-seconds verdict); re-measure ledger; coverage limits; advisory tail as ranked before → after against `/styleguide` (a "looks good as-is" verdict is allowed); a line that seams have no full home in the notes yet, if any seam is found. Re-measure whether the HEAD styleguide (`lib/render-styleguide.js`, `public/styleguide.css`) is itself consistent (run 9 found dark swatches with light hex captions).
3. **Classification rules** (each decided here so the builder does not re-decide):
   * Objective breakage (contrast failure, overflow, unusable layout, unnamed control, zoom lock) → closing comment, ranked, **and** the area note where it traces to a file. Findings 29 and 30 are objective breakage: they were never ticketed, so under the converted template they go to the comment and a note.
   * A defect on a page owned by an in-flight UI ticket (LIN-4008 and children, LIN-4011–4014, LIN-3892, LIN-3490) stays report-only **only if the ticket's text actually covers that finding**. Read the ticket before withholding a note entry. If it does not cover it, it is a note entry.
   * A finding already filed as a ticket stays in the report only, never also in a note.
   * Larger tidy → Waiting entry worded as a size of move, also listed in the closing comment. No area file to cite → closing comment only. Cross-area seam → filed under the area a change would start from, other side named.
   * Subjective design calls → advisory tail only, never the breakage route.
4. **Notes.** Entry format per `docs/areas/README.md` and `LEFTOVER_RULE` (`lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`): area file cited first, this report second, source "Design & Interface Review, 2026-11-08", files never lines. `/swipe` zoom cites `lib/render-swipe.js` first, so it creates `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md` (the registry already defines that slug). A `/styleguide` finding cites `lib/render-styleguide.js` or `public/styleguide.css` first (the registry has no `docs/` pattern). Add the capture-tooling-drift Waiting entry, worded as a size of move, in the area a change would start from. Prune settled or untrue entries in each note touched (the three front-end-browser Waiting entries only if the run shows them settled). `llm-and-prompts.md` and `runs-and-dispatch.md` get no additions unless the same edit prunes at least as much.
5. **Guard and mutation check.** Run `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`; then temporarily swap one entry's first cited path to another area's file and confirm the guard fails (LIN-4387 saw 3 failures), then restore. Every note stays at most 6144 B.
6. **Second-read (Tier 2, fresh-context sub-agent given only the report, the changed-file list and the one question:** "what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"). Post one comment holding the three fields together (verdict, Differed from top finding, Disposition), and copy them with the tier, question and full answer into `## Adversarial Second-Read`. A DISAGREE concludes normally; a "fixed in place" disposition means the report is edited before the PR is final.
7. **Trim evidence** to 10 MB or less: keep JSON, scripts, `coverage-map.md` and only the PNGs the report cites (run 9 §8 did this at 7.2 MB). Open the PR from a branch off `main`, rebased, docs-only; confirm with `git diff --stat origin/main` that only `docs/reviews/` and `docs/areas/` changed.

### Merge and Done authority (LIN-4390)

The template says "merge your own PR"; the dispatch gate reserves merge for review and close-out. Following the LIN-4387 precedent, **build opens the PR green and states that merge is not its to do; review approves; close-out merges pinned to the head commit.** The As-asked block already names this handoff ("name the blocker in the closing comment as an explicit handoff"), so this is delivery of the clause, not a cut, and no human question is needed. If the gate refuses a merge at close-out, the closing comment names it as an explicit handoff.

### Witness for "mints nothing"

A raw count of new identifiers is a false red: LIN-4381 and the coordinator file in parallel. Each stage records, before its session ends, `GET /api/proxy/credential-trail` count of `POST /api/proxy/issues` (expected 0; the 24-hour cap means it must be recorded per session) and confirms no `gh issue create` ran. Baseline: LIN-4391 is the newest identifier; close-out enumerates `LIN-4392` onward and attributes each to its lane. Plan and research sessions: 0 so far.

### Likeliest ways it breaks, each with a witness

1. **A templated image-read.** Witness: the report lists surfaces actually read versus measured only; the second-read is given that list; findings must cite a render or JSON row, and `verify-report-figures.mjs` fails on a figure not in the metrics.
2. **Stale tooling giving wrong "new vs carried" or missing routes.** Witness: `PRIOR` equals `0b4bd287` in the ported file; `differences` in the registry is empty or explained; the route-grep cross-check agrees on added `/getting-started`, backlog and `settings/:area` and the removed `next-run`.
3. **False overflow or false "no overflow".** Witness: every overflow claim names an element with geometry; the `bodyOver:1` styleguide case is resolved either way in the report.
4. **Notes guard failure or a bloated note.** Witness: the guard passes, the mutation check fails when it should, and `wc -c docs/areas/*.md` shows all notes at 6144 B or less.
5. **Counting a parallel lane's issue as this run's.** Witness: per-session trail counts, not the identifier range.

This plan loosens no validation, contract or guard, so no test for a weakened guard is needed beyond the mutation check above.

### Scope check

Behaviour found in other places: the same measure-and-route behaviour lives in the Onboarding & Cold-Start periodical (`lib/periodicals.js`, also renders `routeObjectiveBreakage`). That review owns whether the onboarding journey *completes*; this one owns how `/getting-started` *looks*, so the journey is cited and left to it. No code, config or other docs change; any code defect found is a finding, not a fix.

### Session fit and review

needs multiple sessions: two build sessions, split at a seam where session 1 lands (evidence committed and pushed, counts and limits recorded in `coverage-map.md`) and is verified before session 2 starts, plus review and close-out.

plan-review due: yes

# Research notes: Design & Interface Review run 10 (research stage)

This was research only. I committed nothing, opened no PR and created no issue. The spike used a temporary copy of run 9's tooling inside the repo, which I deleted afterwards (`git status` is clean). The build stage regenerates every figure below.

## 0. Re-grounding (staleness check)

- **Live `main` = `c998cf4c5`**, the same SHA the ticket was minted at. `git log --since=2026-11-08T14:13:42Z` on `lib routes public server.js docs/reviews docs/areas` returns nothing, so the grounding holds at HEAD.
- **Window `0b4bd287..c998cf4c`:** 419 commits. **417 product files** (`lib routes public server.js`): 303 modified, 104 added, 10 deleted. Mapping them through `docs/areas/areas.json` (first match wins) gives the ticket's counts exactly: runs-and-dispatch 75, front-end-pages 74, front-end-browser 73, llm-and-prompts 51, web-routes 37, auth-accounts-and-workspaces 33, agent-api 27, other-features 20, providers 11, platform-and-plumbing 7, reports-and-operator-tools 6, task-model 2, wiring 1.
- The ticket cites both `docs/view-tiers.md` and the features seam. Both docs exist (`docs/view-tiers.md`, `docs/architecture/views.md`), and `featuresParam()` is at `tests/helpers.js` (export at line 47).

## 1. Per-layer audit

### L1. The converted template: what the run must and must not do
- `lib/periodicals.js` `generateDesignReviewPrompt()` renders `periodicalBullet.routeObjectiveBreakage(...)`. That bullet sends objective breakage "to the person in the closing comment … and into the area's note when it traces to a file there; never to a ticket" (`routeObjectiveBreakage`, LIN-4380). `areaNotes(title)` requires one docs-only PR with the report and the note edits, and entries that cite the area file first and the report second, with the source written as "Design & Interface Review, <date>". `conclude()` names the PR and lists any larger tidy and any finding with no area file. `adversarialRead({notes})` sets out the three-field comment.
- **The census guard** is `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`. Its `MINT_WORD` catches ticket and issue filing (close-out fix `56e3cee3`). This pins the *prompt*. It does not pin the *run*, and the run is what this ticket witnesses (see L9).
- The As-asked block is hand-minted (operator note plus grounding) and is consistent with what the template renders. I found no contradiction.

### L2. The area-notes system
- Rules are in `docs/areas/README.md`: two headings (`## Lessons`, `## Waiting`). An entry cites the area's file first and the report second. Cite files, never line numbers. A filed ticket means the item is not also a note entry. "Seams have no full home" (README, plus `areaNotesRoutes()`).
- The guard is `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`. It enforces four rules: the file name is a slug; every cited path exists; the first cited path maps to the note's area; the note is at most 6144 B.
- `LEFTOVER_RULE` is at `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js:24`.
- **Current note sizes (bytes):** front-end-browser 1140, web-routes 970, llm-and-prompts 6118 (26 B of headroom), runs-and-dispatch 6056 (88 B), agent-api 2358, other-features 1803, platform 831, reports 981, wiring 606. **front-end-pages has no note.**
- The registry covers code only. It has no `docs/` pattern (README, "The registry"), so a finding about `/styleguide` cites `lib/render-styleguide.js` (front-end-pages) or `public/styleguide.css` (front-end-browser) first.
- **Precedent:** the P1 converted run, Seams & Tangles run 10 (LIN-4387, PR #2372, merge `82fdb88b`), wrote one Waiting entry each in `docs/areas/other-features.md` and `docs/areas/agent-api.md`. Review ran the guard and mutation-checked it: 17/17 pass, and a swapped first path fails 3 tests. Repeat that check.

### L3. Capture tooling (run 9's scripts, spiked at HEAD)
- The scripts are in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-21/capture/` (26 files). **They resolve paths relative to their own directory** (`EVID = path.resolve(__dirname,'..')` in `census.mjs:29`, `OUT_DIR` in `capture.mjs:44`, `OUT` in `build-registry.mjs:28`) and import product code by a relative path. A copy only works at the same depth: `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>/capture/`. A copy in the scratch area failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND lib/feature-defaults.js`.
- **The spike worked.** `boot-3199.mjs` booted HEAD on :3199 with a scratch data dir. `/`, `/getting-started`, `/styleguide`, `/library`, `/kpis`, `/ship`, `/privacy`, `/templates`, `/archive/1` returned 200 and `/t/nope` returned 404. `capture.mjs landing styleguide settings dispatch tree` gave **24/24 OK in 12.7 s**, including authenticated Settings, Dispatch and Tree through the session seam in both themes. Rendering is cheap. The cost of this review is image-reading and writing.
- **`build-registry.mjs` at HEAD** gives 150 entries and 55 page GET destinations. It records 8 `differences`, which are the new-surface list (see the classes below). It is still pinned to `PRIOR = '6e8bf424'` (line 29), so **repoint it to `0b4bd287`** before trusting the "carried vs new" split.
- **Edits the copy needs:** `PRIOR` (as above); `renderer-args.mjs:15` `TIME = '2026-10-21…'`; curated rows for `/getting-started`, `/workspace/:urlKey/backlog` and `/workspace/:urlKey/settings/:area`, where areas come from `lib/settings-areas.js` (`workspace`, `you`, plus the models area); drop `/workspace/:urlKey/next-run`, which was deleted in the window (`routes/next-run.js`, `lib/render-next-run.js`); sample args for `renderPlainPage`, `renderSignInUnavailablePage` and `renderSourceErrorPage`; the live-console experimental-tag drift; `capture.mjs`'s surface keys, which still list `next-run`.
- **Lighthouse is not installed locally.** `beat2.mjs:32` hardcodes `/Users/work/.npm/_npx/…/lighthouse`, a path from another machine. Use `LIGHTHOUSE_CLI` or `npx lighthouse@12.8.2`, the version run 9 used for comparability. Playwright chromium builds 1181, 1208 and 1228 are cached.
- **Measurement cautions carried from run 9 still apply.** Dark mode honours the `theme` cookie rather than `prefers-color-scheme` on app pages. `overflow-x: clip` makes `scrollWidth` vacuous, so use the geometry rule (`metrics.mjs` OVERFLOW_JS/CLIP_JS). PNGs are quantised, so take colour from the JSON. One spike hint: `/styleguide` at 390 reports `bodyOver: 1` with **no offenders** in both themes. That is probably sub-pixel. Verify it before calling it overflow.

### L4. Session and seed seams
- `/test/set-session` (`routes/test.js:264`) and `/test/set-local-session` (shared helper, `routes/test.js:68`) are wrapped by `createSession()`/`seedLocalWorkspace()` (`tests/helpers.js`, `tests/fixtures/local-harness.js`).
- `/test/set-merge-conflict-session` (`routes/test.js:480`) still seeds only `linear`. So non-Linear merge consent is **synthetic only**, and LIN-3760 is still Backlog. Carry this as a named limit and do not fake it.
- The task page under the Linear mock returned 503 in run 9 (§6 "Additional limits"). The 200 states come from the local-provider seam.

### L5. Surfaces that changed in the window (render these first)
- **The page-route diff** (git grep of `router|app.get` excluding `/api/`, `0b4bd287` against HEAD) shows four changes. Added: `/getting-started` (plus `.md`), `/workspace/:urlKey/backlog`, `/workspace/:urlKey/settings/:area`. Removed: `/workspace/:urlKey/next-run`.
- **New front-end-pages files (20):** `lib/components/{decision-panel,dispatch-no-job,halt-controls,head-meta,model-change-lines,plain-page,settings-ask,settings-frame,settings-group,settings-key-row,settings-row,settings-spend-bar,tabs,time}.js`, `lib/render-settings-{models,workspace,you}.js`, `lib/settings-areas.js`, `lib/settings-copy-first-card.js`, `lib/task-board-view.js`.
- **New front-end-browser files (8):** `public/{cost-format,decision-panel,home-placement,landing-copy,settings-models}.js`, `public/run-control.css`, `public/stage-track.css`, `public/logo/og-image.png` (the social card from `head-meta.js`, which no viewport capture shows).
- **New web-routes files (17):** mostly splits of dashboard and workspace-API routes, plus `routes/getting-started.js` and `routes/settings.js`/`settings-model.js`.
- **Visual specs added in the window:** `tests/visual/lin-4024-home-screenshots.spec.js`, `lin-4103…lin-4117-*.spec.js`. They show which states the Home and type rebuilds considered important. Use them to seed states, but never trust their committed PNGs.

### L6. Ledger of prior findings and tickets (status read today)
- **Done; re-measure that the fix held:** LIN-3761 (Library table clip), LIN-3762 (archive muted tier), LIN-3763 (dark UA links and controls), LIN-3119 (dark `.action-btn`), LIN-739 (landing CTA teal), LIN-3121 (upstream prose).
- **Open; cite and re-measure, do not re-flag:** LIN-3123, LIN-3120, LIN-849 (focus ring and CTA AA; still Backlog even though LIN-739 is Done, so re-measure the teal on *every* door, not only the landing), LIN-3760, LIN-3957, LIN-3960, LIN-3802, LIN-3803, LIN-3997, LIN-4339, LIN-2740.
- **The grounding omits two items run 9 named as "the first candidates next run":** finding 29 (unnamed form controls on Settings, with 2 missing labels and 5 unnamed selects, and 1 unnamed select on Proxy) and finding 30 (`/swipe` has `user-scalable=no`). **Finding 30 still reproduces in source:** `lib/render-swipe.js:144` `viewport: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no'`. Both were never ticketed, so under the converted template they become **objective breakage**: they go to the closing comment and to a note (WCAG 1.4.4 for 30, 4.1.2 for 29). Settings was rebuilt in the window, so finding 29 must be re-measured on the new `settings/:area` pages.
- **"A1–A8" is ambiguous.** Run 9 §10's tail has 8 numbered items, while run 9 §3 also uses A1/A3/A4/A5/A10/A13/A14, which are the 09-26 IDs. I read the ticket's A1–A8 as §10 items 1–8. The report should say that it is using this reading.
- **UI work in flight (filed tickets, so report-only, not notes):** LIN-4008 (UI finish goal, 15 children), LIN-4011 and LIN-4012 (In Progress), LIN-4013 and LIN-4014 (Backlog), LIN-3892 (sweep, 23 children) and LIN-3490 (charter). A defect on a page one of these owns is cited to it.

### L7. Design-system baseline
- `/styleguide` is rendered by `lib/render-styleguide.js` with `public/styleguide.css`. The open baseline tickets are LIN-3957 and LIN-3960. Run 9 found dark swatches captioned with light hex values; that was its advisory 5, and it needs re-checking. `styleguide.css` changed in the window. Measure "does the UI use its own system" against the HEAD styleguide, not against run 9's.

### L8. Merge and Done authority
- LIN-4390 is **Todo** and unresolved. The prompt says the run merges, but the dispatch gate reserves merge for review and close-out. Precedent: LIN-4387 build stated "merge is not mine under the dispatch" and opened the PR green; review then approved and close-out merged pinned (`--match-head-commit`). The As-asked block already covers this ("If the gate refuses your merge, that is the 'genuinely impossible' case … name the blocker in the closing comment as an explicit handoff"). Following the precedent is therefore **not a cut**.

### L9. The witness ("created zero issues"): pinning the measurement
- **A naive count gives a false red.** "How many issues appeared after LIN-4391" picks up parallel lanes: LIN-4381 (P3) runs concurrently and the coordinator files follow-ups. The proxy's issue shape has no creator field.
- **A per-session measurement works.** `GET /api/proxy/credential-trail?windowMs=…` lists this token's own calls by method and route pattern. I checked it on this session, which shows 1 PATCH and 0 `POST /api/proxy/issues`. Each stage that writes (research, build, review, close-out) records its own trail count of `POST /api/proxy/issues` before it ends. The window is capped at 24 h, so record it at the end of each session. **Baseline:** LIN-4391 is the newest identifier now (LIN-4392 to LIN-4395 do not resolve). At close, enumerate `LIN-4392..` and attribute each issue to its lane. Also confirm that no `gh issue create` was run, since a GitHub issue would bypass the proxy trail.

### L10. Sibling surfaces and altitude
- Onboarding & Cold-Start also renders `routeObjectiveBreakage` (`lib/periodicals.js` ~line 886) and owns whether the onboarding journey *completes*. This review owns how it *looks*. `/getting-started` is new and falls on that seam, so cite rather than own anything about journey completion.
- The designer's gap review (`docs/reviews/ui-design-gap-review-2026-10-26/`, grounded at `d3f6785`) is a comparison input. Its findings are mostly already tracked under LIN-4008 and its children. Check what landed since and do not re-flag it.

## 2. Close the set: what I searched to bound the layers
- **Surfaces:** the registry builder, which greps live routes, renderers, archives and experimental views, returned 150 entries with 8 differences (listed in the description's class list). My independent route-diff grep agrees on the 3 added routes and 1 removed route.
- **Seams:** `grep set-.*-session routes/test.js` found 3 seeds, of which only the merge-conflict seed is provider-limited.
- **Notes:** `ls docs/areas` shows nine notes and no front-end-pages note.
- **What I did not check:** emails as actually sent (run 9 rendered `email-*` through renderers), and the guest share link with live data. Both are carried limits in run 9 §6. The set would be wrong if a page is served outside `server.js` and `routes/` (for example a provider basePath router). `build-registry.mjs` already greps `lib/github-install-flow.js` for that reason, so the residual risk is low.

## 3. Options for staging the run
- **A. One build session** does everything: port, capture, census, Lighthouse, image-read, report, notes, second-read and PR. Run 9's full image-read covered about 690 PNGs, and one session risks a templated read (run 9 §6 warns that its sub-reader lines were "pointers to look, not measurements").
- **B. Six beats, as in run 9.** Proven, but the beats existed largely to carry minting and the three-mint cap. The converted template removes that work.
- **C. Two build beats on one branch and one PR (recommended).** **Beat 1:** port the tooling into `_evidence-2026-11-08/capture/` with the edits from L3, then run the registry, full capture (1400/390 × light/dark, plus 320 for the cold and changed surfaces), census, Lighthouse (cold plus about 6 authenticated surfaces) and the re-measure of every L6 item. Commit the evidence and write `coverage-map.md`. **Beat 2:** image-read every changed or new surface and read a sample of the carried ones; write the report (S1–S4, first-experience section, advisory tail before → after); write the notes; run a Tier-2 second-read with a sub-agent; trim the evidence to about 10 MB or less; get the PR green. Then review approves, and close-out merges, posts the closing comment, posts the LIN-4380 and LIN-4349 witness comments, and moves the ticket to Done. **Why:** it separates measuring from judging, as run 9 did, at a third of run 9's overhead, and its merge path matches the LIN-4387 precedent.

## Surface Assessment
Surface Assessment: [improvement noticed, not required: the capture/census/remeasure tooling is copied into each run's evidence folder and hand-edited (PRIOR sha, TIME, curated routes). A durable home for it would stop that drift. This run stays review-only and changes no code, so record it as a Waiting entry worded as a size of move in the area a change would start from, or note it in the report. No subtask.]

A new `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md` is not a second representation, because the registry already defines that slug and the README invites a note per slug. No cut to the As-asked block is proposed, so no DECISION is raised.

## Area notes that bear on this work
- `docs/areas/README.md` (LIN-4347/4371): cite files, never lines; area file first, report second; a filed ticket means no note entry; seams have no full home.
- `docs/areas/web-routes.md` Waiting `routes/test.js` (fold `/test/clear-*`, split the file): this is context only, because the run reads that seam and does not change it.
- `docs/areas/front-end-browser.md`: its three Waiting entries are code shape (Home DOMParser, model-option merge, the brief/recap reader). Prune them only if this run shows them settled.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. Built as written, the plan delivers the whole ask. Its premises check out at HEAD, and every gap I found is a detail the builder can fix without changing the plan's route.

**How the plan meets what was asked.** The plan delivers each part of the As-asked block: *"a converted corrective template must file no tickets; one docs-only PR touching docs/reviews and docs/areas; objective breakage in the closing comment. Record the run on LIN-4380 and LIN-4349"*. Nothing is narrowed. The ask says *"This task owns merging its own report PR … merge it before Done"*. The plan has the task's own close-out stage merge the PR, pinned, before Done. That is still this task merging, and if the gate refuses, the ask's own handoff clause covers it. So it is not a cut.

**What I checked (at `c998cf4c5`; `origin/main` has not moved, and nothing has landed since the ticket was created at 14:13Z)**
- Run 9's tooling is at `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-21/capture/`: 26 files. `build-registry.mjs:29` has `PRIOR='6e8bf424'`. `renderer-args.mjs:15` has `TIME='2026-10-21…'`. `beat2.mjs:32` hardcodes `/Users/work/.npm/_npx/…/lighthouse` behind a `LIGHTHOUSE_CLI` override. Five scripts still carry `next-run` keys (`capture.mjs`, `capture-gap.mjs`, `build-registry.mjs`, `beat3-surfaces.mjs`, `remeasure.mjs`). `routes/next-run.js` and `lib/render-next-run.js` were deleted in the window. All of this matches the plan.
- Run 9 §2 rows 29 and 30, and the eight items in §10, read as the plan says. `lib/render-swipe.js:144` still sets `user-scalable=no`. Run 9 cited `:596`, so the line has moved.
- `/workspace/:urlKey/settings/:area` is at `routes/settings.js:411`. `renderProxyPage` is still served (`server.js:4214`), so Proxy remains a surface to re-measure.
- Area notes. `areas.json` maps `lib/render-*.js`, `lib/components/*` and `lib/settings-areas.js` to `front-end-pages`, and that area has no note yet. The guard (`tests/unit/area-notes.test.js`) enforces the four checks the plan relies on. Note sizes are as the plan states (6118 and 6056 B, cap 6144). The README confirms there is no `docs/` mapping.
- The trail endpoint exists (`routes/proxy-reads.js:364`). An issue create resolves a credential, so it lands as a `provider-lane` row and the endpoint can see it.
- Sequencing holds up: measure, then judge, then review, then close-out. The safeguards hold too: the plan loosens no guard, and it mutation-checks the notes guard.

**Notes for the builder (none block)**
1. **The zero-mint witness has two silent caps.** `GET /api/proxy/credential-trail` defaults to a 15-minute window and returns at most **100** rows, newest first (`lib/proxy-events.js`: `CREDENTIAL_TRAIL_MAX_LIMIT = 100`, window capped at 24 h). Call it with `?windowMs=86400000&limit=100`. If it returns 100 items, the count is not exhaustive, because an early `POST /api/proxy/issues` may have dropped out of view. In that case, say so and lean on the identifier enumeration from `LIN-4392` onward. Treat that enumeration, attributed per lane, as the primary evidence and the trail count as corroboration. The trail is also keyed on the proxy token. If parallel lanes share the local proxy's token, its count includes them. That can only give a false red, which the enumeration resolves.
2. **Enumerate settings areas from `AREAS[].id`, not `AREA_GROUPS`.** The research comment lists "`workspace`, `you`, plus the models area", but `workspace` and `you` are groups. At HEAD there are 8 areas: `sources`, `models`, `running`, `agent-access`, `health`, `change-log`, `features`, `account`. Finding 29's re-measure covers all 8, plus Proxy.
3. **Don't force the capture-tooling-drift Waiting entry.** `docs/areas/README.md` says an entry about a doc or script "cites the code that owns it first". The only honest owner I can find is `lib/periodicals.js`, the prompt that tells runs to reuse run 9's scripts. That file is in `llm-and-prompts`, which has 26 B of headroom, so the entry needs an equal prune in the same edit. If you can't make that citation honestly, route the item to the closing comment as a larger tidy with no area file to cite, and keep it in the report. Treat Session 2 step 4's "Add the … entry" as conditional on that, as the plan's own open question already implies.
